title: Find a Pattern in Event Logs
real_world_story: A security monitoring system receives large log messages and needs to detect whether a known event pattern or alert signature appears within the incoming log stream.

real_world_connection.system: Real-time log monitoring and alert detection system
real_world_connection.input_represents: A log stream and a suspicious event pattern
real_world_connection.target_represents: All positions where the monitored pattern occurs
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Efficiently locating a pattern in a large log stream using prefix information

problem_statement: Given a log string and a target pattern, find all starting indices where the pattern occurs in the log. Overlapping occurrences must also be included.
task: Search the event log for every occurrence of the specified pattern and print its zero-based starting indices.
input_format: The first line contains the log string. The second line contains the pattern to search for.
output_format: Print all zero-based starting indices of the pattern separated by spaces. If the pattern does not occur, print -1.
constraints: Log and pattern contain lowercase English letters

examples.explanation: The pattern 'alert' starts at indices 5 and 10 in the log.
The pattern occurs at indices 0, 2, and 4, including overlapping occurrences.

expected_algorithm.name: KMP Pattern Matching
expected_algorithm.reason: KMP uses prefix information to avoid unnecessary comparisons and efficiently locate alert patterns in large log streams.

hint: Build the Longest Prefix Suffix array for the pattern.
Scan the log while keeping track of the matched pattern length.
After finding a match, use the prefix table to continue searching for overlapping matches.
real_world_takeaway: KMP allows monitoring systems to detect known event signatures efficiently even when log streams become very large.
